What Sets Us Apart

Not a brokerage.
Not a portal.
An advisory firm.

Most Nigerian real estate firms compete to list the most properties. We compete to verify the fewest - because rigour, not volume, is what protects your capital.

Fair Deal Properties is Nigeria's first firm to authentically combine real estate agency, investment advisory, and financial facilitation in a single structured engagement model. One firm. Full lifecycle support. No gaps between the deal and the advice.

Our Operating Principles

Verified Opportunities Only

Every listing passes our full verification standard - site visit, document inspection, ownership cross-check - before it reaches any client.

Advisory-Backed Capital Decisions

You make investment decisions with structured guidance, not sales pressure. We earn your trust before we earn your commission.

Post-Transfer Stewardship

Our engagement doesn't end at title transfer. Continued stewardship, monitoring, and advisory support are built into every client relationship.

Diaspora-Grade Safeguards

Remote transaction management, document custody, on-the-ground presence - purpose-built for investors who cannot be physically present.

The Problems We Solve

Real anxieties.
Direct answers.

We built our advisory model around the concerns clients bring to us - not around what makes transactions easier for us.

"Fake listings and unverified sellers
Every opportunity has been physically verified - site visit, document inspection, and ownership cross-check - before it is presented to any client.
"Title ambiguity and document risk
An independent title search is conducted on every transaction. You receive a written verification report from our legal team before a single naira moves.
"Financing uncertainty and poor structuring
We assess your financing requirements early and facilitate introductions to appropriate providers - with full transparency on terms and obligations.
"No trusted presence on the ground
Diaspora clients are assigned a named advisor who manages the entire transaction remotely and reports regularly post-transfer.
"No post-transaction support whatsoever
Our engagement does not end at closing. We provide continued advisory, rental facilitation referrals, and asset monitoring post-transfer.
"Agents disappear after fees are collected
You will always have a named advisor at Fair Deal Properties - accountable, reachable, and invested in the outcome. Not a call centre.

About Fair Deal Properties

Built on the conviction that your capital deserves more than a listing.

Fair Deal Properties Ltd is an integrated real estate, PropTech and transaction facilitation company delivering trusted property solutions through professional expertise, digital innovation, verified market intelligence and funding advisory.

Fair Deal Properties Ltd
Institutional discipline, applied to private property advisory.
Our Mission

Structure. Verification.
Stewardship.

We exist to serve buyers, investors, developers, and diaspora Nigerians who are serious about property as capital - not just as a place to live.

We are a technology-enabled real estate agency and transaction facilitation firm. We combine professional advisory, verified property opportunities, digital platforms and market intelligence to make property transactions more transparent, efficient, secure and accessible. Technology is our strategic enabler - the means by which we differentiate service, improve client experience and reduce transaction risk across how property is marketed, acquired, developed, financed, managed and experienced.

Nigeria's property market has tremendous opportunity but real structural hazards: fake listings, title ambiguity, weak due diligence, and financing uncertainty. Our model is built explicitly to navigate and neutralise each of these on your behalf - with institutional rigour applied to every transaction we touch.

Our Operating Principles

  • We list nothing we have not independently verified.
  • Title clarity is non-negotiable - always.
  • Advisory precedes every transaction.
  • Diaspora clients receive dedicated stewardship - without exception.
  • Post-transaction support is part of the engagement, not an add-on.
  • Integrity before incentive - always.
Our Values

How we operate - every time.

Integrity Before Incentive

Our advisory is not commission-driven. We are structured to prioritise what is right for you, not what earns us the fastest fee. Our reputation is built on this commitment.

Precision Over Speed

Every verified opportunity demands rigorous review. We would rather lose a listing than compromise our verification standard for urgency. Good decisions take proper time.

Transparency as Infrastructure

You will know what we know. No hidden fees, no undisclosed relationships, no selective omissions. Transparency is the foundation of every client relationship we build.

Long-Term Partnership

Our relationship does not end at title transfer. We are invested in the performance and protection of your asset for years beyond the transaction. This is who we are.

Our Services

Five ways we structure and protect every client engagement.

Each service has been designed around the real challenges clients face in Nigeria's property market - not around what is easiest for us to offer.

Service One

Real Estate Agency & Transaction Facilitation

End-to-end transaction management, not just introductions.

We manage the complete transaction lifecycle - from opportunity identification and site inspection to offer negotiation, legal documentation, and title transfer. Our involvement provides a structured layer of discipline that protects your interest at every stage. We work only with verified listings, ensuring no transaction begins without clear documentary evidence of title and ownership.

Speak to an Advisor

What's Included

  • Pre-market opportunity sourcing
  • Independent market price analysis
  • Offer structuring and negotiation
  • Legal coordination and document review
  • Title transfer support and post-close monitoring
Service Two

Real Estate Investment Advisory

Capital allocation counsel, not commission-driven brokerage.

Our investment advisory service is structured for clients who approach property as a capital decision - not just a lifestyle purchase. We provide market intelligence, opportunity analysis, and structured guidance to help you build a considered position in the Nigerian property market. Our advisory is not commission-driven - it is built around your outcome.

Speak to an Advisor

What's Included

  • Market intelligence and sector outlook
  • Investment thesis development
  • Opportunity screening and shortlisting
  • Risk and return analysis
  • Portfolio composition guidance
Service Three

Bridge-Financing Facilitation & Financial Advisory

Connecting capital-ready buyers with structured financing channels.

Financing is often the single largest barrier to completing a sound property transaction. We facilitate access to bridge-financing solutions and maintain relationships with credible lending partners. We do not lend - but we advise, introduce, and structure. Our role is to help you access the right financing instrument for your situation, with full transparency on terms and obligations.

  • Lender introductions and facilitation

  • Debt structure advisory

How It Works

A structured process. No ambiguity at any stage.

From first conversation to post-transfer stewardship - six disciplined steps that govern every engagement, every time. No shortcuts. No surprises.

The Engagement Process
Six steps. No ambiguity at any stage.
01
Confidential Consultation

A structured advisory session - in person, by video, or by phone - to understand your goals, timeline, risk profile, budget, and specific constraints. We listen before we recommend. This session is obligation-free and completely confidential.

02
Opportunity Screening & Mandate Definition

We identify and screen opportunities against your defined mandate - from our verified platform and off-market sources. You receive only what passes our standard. This is curated shortlisting, not mass listing distribution.

03
Independent Due Diligence

Before any commitment is made, we conduct an independent title search, document review, site verification, and developer assessment where applicable. You receive a written verification report from our legal team. No naira moves before this report is delivered and reviewed.

04
Offer Structuring & Negotiation

We represent your interest at the negotiating table - structuring the offer, negotiating terms, managing counterparty expectations, and ensuring your contractual protections are embedded in every agreement. You never negotiate alone.

05
Legal Coordination & Title Transfer

Full legal coordination - Deed of Assignment drafting, Governor's Consent, title registration where applicable, payment milestone management, and final handover. Every document is verified before it is executed. Every payment is tracked and confirmed.

06
Post-Transfer Stewardship

The engagement does not end at title transfer. We provide continued advisory, asset monitoring, rental facilitation referrals, and quarterly intelligence reports for as long as you hold the asset. Your investment is our long-term responsibility.

Financing Advisory

We don't lend. We ensure you borrow right.

Financing is often the single largest barrier to a sound property transaction. We advise, introduce, and structure - with full transparency on terms and obligations, always.

Financing Routes

Our Financing Advisory Service

Structure before you commit.

We assess your financing requirements early in the advisory process - before you are in negotiation and under pressure. Our role is to ensure you never commit to financing terms you don't fully understand.

We maintain relationships with credible bridge-financing providers across Nigeria's formal and informal capital markets. We introduce only where the terms are transparent, the provider is credible, and the structure serves your long-term interest - not theirs.

Frequently Asked Questions

Real questions. Honest answers.

We believe an informed client is our best client. Here are the questions we hear most often - answered with the directness and clarity every client deserves.

We are Nigeria's only firm that genuinely combines real estate agency with independent financial advisory in a single integrated engagement. We are not commission-only brokers. Every listing is independently verified before presentation. We have a dedicated diaspora advisory service. And our engagement continues post-transfer - not just until the commission is paid. Most critically: we list nothing we have not physically inspected and legally verified. This is not standard practice in Nigeria's market. It is our non-negotiable standard.
Our verification process involves three steps: a physical site inspection conducted by our team (not delegated to third parties), a full document review (C of O, R of O, Survey Plans, Deed of Assignment chains), and an independent title search through our legal team with the relevant land registry. 'Title verified' means we have confirmed, in writing, that the title documents presented are genuine, that the ownership claim is supported by the registry records, and that there are no encumbrances or adverse claims we have been able to identify. You receive a written verification report before any commitment is made.
Yes - fully. Our Diaspora Advisory Package is specifically built for remote transactions. We have completed multiple transactions for clients in the UK, USA, Canada, and Europe without a single Nigeria visit required. We conduct the site inspection, manage the legal process, handle document custody, facilitate payments through secure channels, and provide video/photo evidence at every milestone. Many clients choose to visit post-transfer (to see their asset), but it is never required for the transaction itself.
We are transparent about our compensation model because opacity in this area is one of our industry's biggest problems. We earn advisory fees and transaction facilitation fees, which are discussed and agreed in writing before any engagement begins. We do not receive undisclosed commissions from sellers or developers. Where we receive fees from both sides of a transaction, this is disclosed to both parties in advance. Our advisory-first model means our interests are aligned to your outcome - not to closing the fastest transaction at any cost.
We do not lend. We are not a financial institution and we do not hold or deploy capital on behalf of clients. Our financing advisory service involves needs assessment, lender introductions, term review and guidance, and deal structuring - all on an advisory basis. We maintain relationships with credible bridge-financing providers and can facilitate introductions where appropriate, ensuring you understand every term before you commit. This distinction - advising on financing rather than providing it - is important to maintaining our independence and our clients' trust.
No. Post-transfer stewardship is part of our engagement, not an optional add-on. After title transfer, we continue to monitor your asset on the ground, provide quarterly market intelligence relevant to your holding, facilitate rental management referrals if you choose to let the property, and remain available for advisory on future disposal, reinvestment, or financing decisions. Your investment continues for years after the transaction - and so do we.
Our primary markets are Abuja (where we are headquartered), Lagos, and Port Harcourt. We operate actively and have on-ground verification capability in all three cities. For diaspora clients, we serve investors from the UK, USA, Canada, Europe, Middle East, and other jurisdictions. We do not claim to cover markets we cannot properly serve - if you are looking at an opportunity outside our active markets, we will tell you directly and help you identify the right local advisory resource.

How the Fair Deal platform is engineered, how your data is protected, and the regulatory framework we operate within.

Architecture & Controls
Buy what is solved. Build only the moat.
Architecture

The technology stack

We buy proven infrastructure and build only what differentiates us. Our engineering effort goes into verification workflow and matching logic - not into rebuilding solved problems.

Client Layer
Next.js / ReactProgressive Web AppWhatsApp Business APIMobile-first responsive

Nigeria is mobile-first and WhatsApp-native. Our primary client interface is built for a phone on an intermittent connection, not a desktop on fibre.

Application
Node.js APIPostgreSQLRedis cacheRole-based access control

A single source of truth for listings, verifications, transactions and client records - with strict role separation between advisory, verification and finance functions.

Intelligence
Vector embeddingsLLM-assisted draftingHuman-in-the-loop review

AI drafts, structures and matches. A named human verifies every factual assertion. No verification finding, title status or property condition is ever machine-generated.

Document Vault
Encrypted object storageAES-256 at restTLS 1.3 in transitImmutable audit log

Every document access is logged with actor, timestamp and purpose. Diaspora clients can verify who touched their records and when.

Payments
Licensed PSP railsThird-party escrowNo custody of client funds

Transaction funds move directly between counterparties or through licensed escrow. Fair Deal Properties never holds client purchase funds - a structural safeguard, not a policy preference.

Integrations
Lender submission portalsE-signatureVirtual tour captureAnalytics
Data Protection

How your information is protected

NDPA 2023 Compliance

We process personal data as a Data Controller under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, with a lawful basis identified for every processing activity. Our full Privacy Notice sets out your data subject rights and how to exercise them.

Access Segregation

Verification staff, advisory staff and finance staff hold separate permissions. No single role can originate, verify and approve the same transaction - the same control principle applied in financial services.

Audit Trail Integrity

Verification findings, document access and transaction milestones are written to an append-only log. Records can be added to and read, but not silently altered or deleted.

Retention Discipline

Transaction records retained 7 years, KYC records 5 years post-relationship, in line with Nigerian tax and AML obligations. Enquiry data not converted to engagement is purged after 2 years.

Regulatory Framework

The rules we operate under

We would rather state our regulatory boundaries plainly than let a client assume we do something we are not authorised to do.

Framework
What It Means For You
MLPPA 2022 & SCUML
Real estate businesses are designated non-financial institutions. All clients complete KYC verification before engagement. We are required to report suspicious transactions without prior notice to the client.
NDPA 2023 / NDPC
Registered data controller obligations, data subject rights honoured within 30 days, and mandatory breach notification.
ESVARBON
We do not offer valuation services. Formal property valuation is reserved to registered Estate Surveyors and Valuers. Where a valuation is required we engage a registered firm on your behalf. Our market analytics are decision intelligence, clearly distinguished from valuation.
Mortgage Facilitation
We facilitate and advise on mortgage arrangements with licensed institutions. We are not a lender, we do not originate credit in our own name, and we do not take deposits or hold client funds.

On AI and honesty: We use artificial intelligence to draft documents, structure data, match opportunities and automate follow-up. We do not use it to generate verification findings, title conclusions, property condition assessments or client testimonials. In a market where anyone can now generate a convincing listing, the scarce asset is a person who actually visited the site and put their name to what they found. That is what we sell.

Article 1

Who we are and what this notice covers

Fair Deal Properties Ltd ("Fair Deal Properties", "we", "us") is a company registered in the Federal Republic of Nigeria with its office at No. 4 Ekeh A. Yesufu Close, Utako, Abuja, Federal Capital Territory. We are a technology-enabled real estate agency and transaction facilitation firm.

We act as a data controller in respect of the personal data described in this notice. Where we engage service providers who process personal data on our instruction, they act as data processors and are bound by a written data processing agreement.

This notice applies to everyone whose personal data we process: visitors to this website, people who make enquiries, clients, prospective clients, members of cooperative societies we work with, sub-agents, developers, professional panel members and suppliers.

It is written in plain language. The General Application and Implementation Directive 2025 requires that information given to data subjects be clear, taking into account vulnerable individuals. If any part of this notice is unclear to you, contact our Data Protection Officer and we will explain it.

Article 2

The law we operate under

Our processing is governed by:

  • The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 (NDPA), the principal statute.
  • The Nigeria Data Protection Act General Application and Implementation Directive 2025 (GAID), issued by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission on 20 March 2025 and effective from 19 September 2025, which replaced the Nigeria Data Protection Regulation 2019 and its Implementation Framework.
  • The Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act 2022, which imposes customer due diligence and record-keeping obligations on real estate businesses as designated non-financial businesses and professions.
  • Other Nigerian legislation imposing record-keeping or disclosure obligations on us, including tax legislation.
Article 3

Personal data we collect

We collect only what we need for the purposes set out at Article 4. The categories are:

  • Identity data - full name, former names, date of birth, nationality, country of residence, photograph, and government identification numbers including Bank Verification Number, National Identification Number and passport or licence particulars where required for customer due diligence.
  • Contact data - residential and correspondence address, email address, telephone and WhatsApp number.
  • Financial data - income particulars, employment or business details, bank statements, existing obligations, source of funds declarations, equity contribution evidence, and tax particulars, where you engage us for mortgage facilitation or where customer due diligence requires it.
  • Transaction data - property preferences, budget, timeline, intended use, offers made, properties viewed, documents held on your behalf, and the record of your engagement with us.
  • Due diligence data - the outcome of politically exposed person screening, risk rating, and any enhanced due diligence we conduct.
  • Technical data - internet protocol address, browser type and version, device identifiers, pages visited, time spent and referral source, collected through this website.
  • Communications data - correspondence, consultation notes, and records of calls and messages between you and your named advisor.

Sensitive personal data. We do not seek sensitive personal data and do not require it for our services. Where any sensitive personal data is disclosed to us incidentally, we process it only where a lawful basis under the NDPA applies, and we will tell you which.

Children. The General Application and Implementation Directive 2025 defines a child as a person under 18 years of age. Our services are directed exclusively to adults. We do not knowingly collect personal data from a child. Where we become aware that we hold such data without the consent of a parent or guardian, we delete it.

Article 4

Why we process your data, and our lawful basis

We process personal data only where a lawful basis under the NDPA applies. Each purpose and its basis is set out below.

Where we rely on legitimate interest, we have assessed that interest against your rights and freedoms and concluded that it does not override them. You may ask us for that assessment.

Article 5

Where your data comes from

From you directly - when you complete a form on this site, contact us by email, telephone or WhatsApp, attend a consultation or site visit, or enter into an engagement.

From third parties with your knowledge - referral partners, cooperative societies of which you are a member, developers or professional introducers.

Automatically - through cookies and similar technologies on this website, subject to your consent for any non-essential category.

From public sources - the Corporate Affairs Commission, land registries, court registries and published professional directories, for verification and due diligence.

Article 6

Who we share your data with

We do not sell personal data and we do not share it for any third party’s own marketing. We share only as follows, and only to the extent necessary:

  • Legal practitioners we instruct on your behalf for title investigation and conveyancing.
  • Registered Estate Surveyors and Valuers we instruct where a formal valuation is required.
  • Financing institutions - Primary Mortgage Banks, the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria, participating commercial banks and other lenders - where you instruct us to submit an application, and only with your consent and only what the institution requires.
  • Licensed escrow providers, where an escrow arrangement is used.
  • Regulatory and law enforcement authorities - including the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, the Special Control Unit against Money Laundering, the Nigeria Financial Intelligence Unit and the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission - where required by law.
  • Service providers who process on our instruction under a written data processing agreement, including secure hosting, document storage, communications and accounting providers.
  • Our professional advisers, including auditors and insurers, under obligations of confidence.

Where we are required to make a report under the Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act 2022, we are prohibited by that Act from notifying you of the report.

Article 7

Transfers of your data outside Nigeria

Because we serve diaspora clients and use cloud infrastructure, your personal data may be transferred to or accessed from outside Nigeria, including the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, the European Union and the United Arab Emirates.

Under the NDPA and the General Application and Implementation Directive 2025, a transfer outside Nigeria requires an adequate safeguard or an applicable lawful basis. Where we transfer your data we rely on one of the following, and we will tell you which applies to you on request:

  • A determination by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission that the destination country provides an adequate level of protection.
  • Contractual safeguards binding the recipient to standards equivalent to those required under the NDPA.
  • Your explicit consent, given after we have informed you of the possible risks of the transfer in the absence of an adequacy determination or other safeguard.
  • Necessity for the performance of a contract with you, or for steps taken at your request before entering a contract.

We do not transfer personal data to any recipient that will not accept these obligations.

Article 8

How long we keep your data

We keep personal data no longer than is necessary for the purpose for which it was collected, except where a longer period is required by law or to establish or defend a legal claim.

Cross-border transfer

Where your data is held, and why it leaves Nigeria

Your personal data is stored on infrastructure operated by Amazon Web Services in the Republic of Ireland (eu-west-1). Amazon Web Services operates no data centre in Nigeria, so storing your data with it necessarily transfers that data outside Nigeria.

We make that transfer on the basis in section 41(1)(a) of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023: the recipient is bound by a law which provides an adequate level of protection. That law is Regulation (EU) 2016/679, the General Data Protection Regulation, which is in force in Ireland and which binds Amazon Web Services in respect of data it holds there. We rely in addition on the contractual clauses in our data processing addendum with Amazon Web Services, which is an independent basis under the same section.

We have recorded the legal basis for this transfer and our assessment of the adequacy of protection, as section 41(2) requires. We have also carried out a data protection impact assessment for this transfer, which Article 28(3)(o) of the General Application and Implementation Directive 2025 makes mandatory. Both are available to you, and to the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, on request.

We have not asserted, and do not rely on, any adequacy decision issued by the Commission in respect of Ireland. Whether the Commission has issued one is a matter for the Commission.

If you would prefer that your data not be transferred, tell us before you submit anything. We can take your instructions by telephone or in person and hold the record outside this website.

Article 9

Your rights

Under the NDPA you have the following rights. We do not charge for exercising them. The Act requires us to act without undue delay and does not fix a number of days; we commit to responding within 30 days as a matter of our own standard. Where a request is complex we may extend that period, and we will tell you why before the original period expires.

  • Right to be informed - to know what we do with your data. This notice is how we discharge it.
  • Right of access - to obtain a copy of the personal data we hold about you and information about how we use it.
  • Right to rectification - to have inaccurate or incomplete data corrected or completed without undue delay.
  • Right to erasure - to have your data deleted where it is no longer necessary, where you withdraw consent and no other basis applies, or where it has been unlawfully processed. This right does not override our legal retention obligations.
  • Right to restriction - to limit our processing while a dispute about accuracy or lawfulness is resolved.
  • Right to data portability - to receive data you provided to us in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format, and to have it transmitted to another controller where technically feasible.
  • Right to object - to object to processing based on legitimate interest, and to object to direct marketing at any time, with no exception.
  • Right to withdraw consent - at any time, as easily as it was given.
  • Rights in relation to automated decision-making - not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing which produces legal or similarly significant effects. We do not make such decisions. Our opportunity matching produces suggestions for a human advisor; it does not decide anything about you.
  • Right to lodge a complaint - with us, and with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission.
Article 10

How to exercise your rights

Use the Data Subject Rights Request page on this site, or write to our Data Protection Officer at the address below.

We commit to acknowledging within 5 business days and responding fully within 30 days. These are our own published commitments: section 34 of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 requires us to act without constraint or unreasonable delay but sets no number of days, and we would rather tell you what we will actually do than quote you a deadline the Act does not contain. We may ask you to verify your identity before we act, to ensure we do not disclose your data to someone else.

If you are dissatisfied with our response. Article 40(2) and (3) of the General Application and Implementation Directive 2025 allow you to serve a Standard Notice to Address Grievance on us, in the form at Schedule 9 to that Directive. You may use that route with us. Serving it is not a precondition to complaining to the Commission - you may do either, or both. If the matter remains unresolved, you may escalate it to the Nigeria Data Protection Commission or institute civil proceedings. We will not require you to exhaust our internal process before approaching the Commission.

Data Protection Officer

Fair Deal Properties Ltd has appointed a Data Protection Officer in accordance with the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and the General Application and Implementation Directive 2025. The Data Protection Officer is contactable directly and independently of any other function in the firm.

Email: dpo@fairdealng.com  |  Telephone: 09049924198

Post: The Data Protection Officer, Fair Deal Properties Ltd, No. 4 Ekeh A. Yesufu Close, Utako, Abuja, FCT, Nigeria

Article 7 of the General Application and Implementation Directive 2025 requires that data subjects be able to contact the Data Protection Officer and exercise their rights. You may contact the Data Protection Officer about any matter in this notice without going through any other part of the firm.

Article 11

How we protect your data

We apply technical and organizational measures proportionate to the risk, including:

  • Encryption of personal data at rest and in transit.
  • Role-based access control, with verification, advisory and finance functions holding separate permissions.
  • An append-only audit log recording who accessed which document, when and for what purpose. Clients may request their own access log.
  • Segregation of duties, so that no single person can originate, verify and approve the same transaction.
  • Confidentiality obligations and data protection training for every member of staff and every sub-agent.
  • Written data processing agreements with every supplier that processes personal data on our behalf.
  • Periodic review of our security posture and of this notice.

No transmission over the internet is entirely secure. We apply all reasonable measures, but we cannot guarantee absolute security, and we ask you to take care when sending personal information electronically.

Article 12

Data protection impact assessments

Where a processing activity is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects - in particular where it involves new technology, large-scale processing or sensitive personal data - we conduct a Data Protection Impact Assessment before the processing begins, document it, and make it available to the Nigeria Data Protection Commission on request.

Article 13

Personal data breaches

We maintain a breach response procedure. Where a personal data breach occurs, we:

  • Record it in our incident register immediately on becoming aware of it.
  • Assess the risk to affected data subjects without delay.
  • Notify the Nigeria Data Protection Commission within 72 hours of becoming aware, where the breach is notifiable, using the content required by the General Application and Implementation Directive 2025.
  • Notify affected data subjects without undue delay where the breach is likely to result in a high risk to their rights and freedoms, in clear language, describing what happened, what we are doing, and what they should do.
Article 14

Records of processing and compliance reporting

We maintain a record of processing activities covering each processing purpose, the categories of data and data subjects, the lawful basis relied on, recipients, international transfers and safeguards, retention periods and security measures. It is kept current and is available to the Nigeria Data Protection Commission on request.

Where we are designated a Data Controller or Data Processor of Major Importance under Article 9 of the General Application and Implementation Directive 2025, we will register with the Commission, conduct the required data protection audit and file Compliance Audit Returns within the prescribed timelines. Our Data Protection Officer prepares semi-annual internal data protection reports for management.

Our designation status and registration particulars are reviewed against the current thresholds and will be published here once determined.

Article 15

Changes to this notice

We review this notice at least annually and whenever our processing changes materially. The version number and effective date at the top show the current version. Material changes are notified on this website and, where the change affects an existing engagement, directly to the client.

We retain superseded versions and will provide any earlier version on request, so that you can see the terms that applied at the time of your engagement.

Supervisory authority. The Nigeria Data Protection Commission supervises compliance with the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023. You have the right to lodge a complaint with the Commission at any time. We would ask you to raise it with our Data Protection Officer first so that we have the opportunity to put it right, but you are under no obligation to do so.

Article 1

What cookies are

Cookies are small text files placed on your device by a website. They are widely used to make sites work, to remember your preferences, and in some cases to collect information about how a site is used.

This notice also covers technologies that work in a similar way, including web beacons, pixel tags, local storage and session storage. Where we refer to cookies we include all of these.

Article 2

Our consent position

Under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and the General Application and Implementation Directive 2025, consent must be freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous, and must be as easy to withdraw as it is to give. We apply that as follows:

  • No optional cookie is set before you consent. Our consent banner does not pre-tick any category, and closing or ignoring it is not treated as consent.
  • Consent is granular. You may accept one category and refuse another. Accepting all is never required in order to refuse all.
  • Rejecting is as easy as accepting. Both are a single click, presented with equal prominence.
  • Consent is not a condition of use. Every part of this site works whether you accept optional cookies or not.
  • Your consent is recorded. We store what you chose, when, by what method and against which version of this notice, so that we can evidence it. You may view that record at any time using the control above.
  • Withdrawal is always available. The privacy control at the lower left of every page reopens the preference centre.

Legal & Compliance

Your Data Rights

Exercise any right you hold over your personal data under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023. The Act requires us to act without undue delay; we commit to acknowledging within 5 business days and responding within 30 days. There is no charge.

Privacy Notice Cookie Notice Your Data Rights Terms of Service
What you can ask for

Ten rights, and what each one does

  • Be informed - know what we do with your data. Our Privacy Notice discharges this.
  • Access - receive a copy of your data and information about how we use it.
  • Rectification - have inaccurate or incomplete data corrected without undue delay.
  • Erasure - have data deleted where it is no longer necessary or where consent is withdrawn and no other basis applies.
  • Restriction - limit our processing while a dispute about accuracy or lawfulness is resolved.
  • Portability - receive data you gave us in a machine-readable format and have it transmitted onward where feasible.
  • Object - object to processing based on legitimate interest, and to direct marketing at any time without exception.
  • Withdraw consent - at any time, as easily as it was given.
  • Automated decisions - not be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing with legal or similarly significant effect. We make no such decisions.
  • Complain - to us, and to the Nigeria Data Protection Commission.

Where erasure is limited

Some records we are required by law to keep. Customer due diligence records must be retained for 5 years after the end of a business relationship under the Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act 2022, and transaction records for 7 years for tax and professional liability purposes. Where we cannot erase, we will tell you precisely which obligation prevents it and when the data will be deleted.

If you are not satisfied with our response

Article 40(2) and (3) of the General Application and Implementation Directive 2025 allow you to serve a Standard Notice to Address Grievance on us, in the form at Schedule 9 to that Directive. You may use that route with us and we will treat it as a formal grievance. Serving it is not a precondition to complaining to the Nigeria Data Protection Commission - you may do either, or both.

If the matter remains unresolved you may escalate to the Nigeria Data Protection Commission or institute civil proceedings. We will not require you to exhaust our internal process before approaching the Commission.

Submit a request

Completing this form raises a formal data subject request. You will receive a reference number.

Identity verification. We may ask you to verify your identity before we act, so that we do not disclose your personal data to someone else. We will ask for the minimum necessary and will not retain verification documents beyond the request. Where you act on behalf of another data subject, we will require evidence of your authority.

Section 07

Anti-Money Laundering & Compliance Obligations

Fair Deal Properties is subject to and fully committed to compliance with applicable Nigerian anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing legislation, including the Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act 2022 (MLPPA 2022) and the Terrorism (Prevention and Prohibition) Act 2022.

In accordance with these obligations, all clients are required to complete Know-Your-Customer (KYC) verification before any formal engagement commences. We are required by law to:

  • -Verify the identity of all clients and beneficial owners prior to providing services.
  • -Conduct enhanced due diligence on politically exposed persons (PEPs) and high-risk clients.
  • -Report suspicious transactions to the Nigeria Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU) without prior notification to the client (as required by law).
  • -Retain KYC documentation for a minimum of 5 years following the conclusion of the business relationship.

Failure or refusal to complete KYC verification will result in our inability to provide services. We are registered with the Special Control Unit Against Money Laundering (SCUML) as required for real estate businesses in Nigeria.

Section 05

Our operating commitments

Obligation
What we do
Breach notification
Any personal data breach is notified to the NDPC within 72 hours of our becoming aware of it. Where the breach is likely to result in high risk to you, we notify you directly without undue delay, in plain language.
Records of processing
We maintain a Record of Processing Activities covering every processing purpose, its lawful basis, the categories of data and data subjects, recipients, transfers, retention and security measures. It is reviewed quarterly.
Impact assessment
A Data Protection Impact Assessment is carried out before any processing likely to result in high risk, and is documented and retained.
Compliance audit
Where we meet the threshold for a data controller of major importance, we conduct the annual data protection compliance audit and file the Compliance Audit Return through a licensed Data Protection Compliance Organisation.
Direct marketing
We do not send marketing of any kind without your prior consent. Consent to marketing is never bundled with acceptance of our terms or with any other permission, and withdrawing it is a single step.
Processors
No third party processes personal data on our behalf without a written data processing agreement meeting the requirements of the Act. We assess every processor before engagement.
Cross-border transfers
Our diaspora service necessarily involves transfers outside Nigeria. Every transfer is made on a lawful basis recognised by the Act, with documented safeguards, and is recorded in our Record of Processing Activities.

Version control. This page, our Privacy Notice and our Cookie Policy are version-controlled and dated. Where we make a material change we publish it here and, for clients, notify it directly. The version in force is the one displayed. Superseded versions are retained and available on request so you can see what applied when.

We ask before we set any cookie

Fair Deal Properties Ltd uses cookies on this website. Under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and the NDPA General Application and Implementation Directive 2025, cookies that are not strictly necessary require your active consent before they are set. Nothing optional is placed on your device until you choose below. You may decline everything optional and continue using the site normally.

Strictly necessary Always active
Required for the site to function - page navigation, form submission, session continuity and recording your choice on this notice. These are set on the basis of legitimate interest and cannot be disabled. No personally identifying profile is built from them.
Functional and preference
Remembers choices you make - saved properties, the page you were last on, your inspection session reference. Retention up to 12 months. Declining these means the site will not remember your choices between visits.
Analytics and performance
Anonymised information on how the site is used, so we can improve it. Retention up to 24 months. We do not use this to identify you and we do not sell or share it for any third party's own purposes.
Marketing
We do not currently operate advertising or third-party remarketing cookies. If that changes, nothing will be set unless you switch this on. Direct marketing by any channel requires your prior consent and is never bundled with any other permission.
Declining is as easy as accepting and carries no disadvantage. You can change your choices at any time using the Privacy Choices control at the bottom left of any page.
